title: Automated unloading and loading robot system

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: The reference describes a robot with an End of Arm Tool (EoAT) that includes a gripper mechanism, but it does not mention a housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: The reference describes a gripper mechanism that moves between a retracted and extended position, but it does not specify that this mechanism involves a displaceable magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe pole shoes or workpiece contact surfaces in the context of a magnetic gripper.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe pole shoes or their function in guiding a magnetic field.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not describe a workpiece contact surface with a specific angle relative to a displacement direction, as it does not disclose a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: The reference describes a gripper mechanism, but it is not a magnetic gripper with the specified components and contact surface angle.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: The reference describes a gripper mechanism that uses vacuum cups, not a magnetic gripper system with magnetic force.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.quote: Pivotal movement of the mast extension arm 1204 causes the mast 204 along with the EoAT 206 to move horizontally in the longitudinal direction 506 of the robot 102 .
features.note: The reference describes the EoAT moving along a longitudinal direction, but it does not explicitly state that a housing extends along this axis with a magnet's displacement parallel to it.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: The reference does not describe pole shoes or active structures for directing a magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with a bevel or a workpiece contact surface.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with multiple projections for directing a magnetic field or forming a workpiece contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections with recesses between them, as it does not disclose a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.quote: By sensing the edges of the cargo items 110 , the robot 102 is able to properly position the EoAT 206 during stacking and unstacking of the cargo items 110 .
features.note: The reference describes a cargo sensor and robot movement for positioning the EoAT relative to a cargo item, which is a positioning device for a workpiece, but it is not specifically on a magnetic gripper or for positioning a ferromagnetic workpiece on a contact surface.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: The reference does not describe pole shoes or their magnetic polarity.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: The gripper mechanism 2302 is designed to grab the cargo items 110 and pull them onto the EoAT 206 when unloading the cargo items 110 from the cargo carrier 108 or elsewhere.
features.note: The reference describes a gripper mechanism that moves between gripping and release positions, and it mentions electric motors for movement, but it does not specify that the gripper mechanism uses a displaceable magnet.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.quote: This movement of the gripper mechanism 2302 can be sensed by the cargo sensor system 2322 (e.g., the cargo facing sensor 2326 ) and/or other sensors.
features.note: The reference explicitly states that the movement of the gripper mechanism (between gripping and release positions) can be sensed by a cargo sensor system.
features.refuted: The quote describes a cargo sensor system detecting movement of the gripper mechanism, not a position sensor detecting gripping/release positions or a workpiece sensor detecting ferromagnetic workpieces.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.quote: The mast channel 1502 provides a conduit for housing power cabling, communication lines, air hosing, wiring, and other components for the EoAT 206 .
features.note: The reference describes a mast channel acting as a conduit for supply lines to the EoAT, which could be considered a receptacle for supply lines. However, it does not explicitly mention a receptacle for a workpiece sensor within a housing.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.quote: Turning to FIG. 18 , an EoAT pitch-yaw actuator joint 1802 connects the mast 204 to the EoAT 206 .
features.note: The reference describes an EoAT pitch-yaw actuator joint that connects the EoAT to the mast, which functions as an interface for attaching the EoAT (which contains the gripper) to a larger robotic manipulator (the mast and base unit). However, it is not specifically on a magnetic gripper.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not describe any magnetic shielding or suppression of magnetic field escape, as it does not disclose a magnetic gripper.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections or their dimensions relative to a workpiece thickness, as it does not disclose a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.quote: The mast channel 1502 at the end of the mast 204 near the EoAT 206 also houses an EoAT pitch or tilt drive 1612 .
features.note: The reference describes a 'mast channel' which could be interpreted as a groove or receptacle for components, but it is not explicitly in the housing of a magnetic gripper.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with a bevel or a workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with a bevel or a workpiece contact surface.

claims.quote: To sense whether or not cargo items 110 are on the EoAT 206 as well as the relative position of the cargo items 110 , the EoAT 206 includes a cargo sensor system 2322 .
claims.note: The reference discloses a cargo sensor system to detect cargo items, which could be considered a workpiece sensor. However, it does not specify that the workpiece must be ferromagnetic, nor does it explicitly state the sensor is for detecting a 'ferromagnetic workpiece'.

claims.quote: The mast channel 1502 provides a conduit for housing power cabling, communication lines, air hosing, wiring, and other components for the EoAT 206 .
claims.note: The reference describes conduits for housing power cabling, communication lines, and air hosing, which are types of supply lines. However, it does not explicitly mention a receptacle for a workpiece sensor within the housing of the EoAT, though it does mention a cargo sensor system on the EoAT.

claims.quote: FIG. 18 , an EoAT pitch-yaw actuator joint 1802 connects the mast 204 to the EoAT 206 .
claims.note: The reference describes an EoAT pitch-yaw actuator joint that connects the End of Arm Tool (EoAT) to the mast, which functions as a manipulator interface for attaching the gripper (part of the EoAT) to a manipulator (the mast).
